title: Unit – 5 : Session – 7 | Natural Acceptance, Ethical Conduct and Its Analysis
sections: Q1. HUMAN VALUES ARE NATURALLY ACCEPTABLE AND DEFINITE: every human being naturally accepts trust over betrayal, respect over insult, care over neglect — this acceptance needs no external proof and is the SAME for all, across time, place and person. Because this acceptance is anchored in the reality of the Self and co-existence (not in custom or command), the values derived from it are definite: they cannot be revised by fashion, law or market. What changes across cultures is only the FORM of expression (how respect is shown), never the CONTENT (that respect is naturally acceptable).

Q2. VALUE-POLICY-CHARACTER IN ETHICAL CONDUCT: VALUE is the understanding of what is valuable (trust, respect, right utilisation...); POLICY is the definite intention formed from values — to nurture and protect the other (family, society, nature); CHARACTER is the lived consistency — chastity in relationship, right use of wealth, kindness in behaviour and work. Ethical conduct is the visible coherence of the three: where values are understood, policy becomes definite and character steady. A person may know values without policy (understanding without commitment) or hold policy without character (intention without practice) — only the alignment of all three constitutes ethical human conduct.

Q3. ETHICAL CONDUCT IS SELF-SATISFYING, PEOPLE-FRIENDLY, ECO-FRIENDLY: SELF-SATISFYING — it accords with my own natural acceptance, so there is inner harmony, no guilt, no split between belief and behaviour; happiness in continuity. PEOPLE-FRIENDLY — conduct rooted in trust, respect, affection and justice necessarily fulfils the needs of the Self of others; it can nurture but never exploit. ECO-FRIENDLY — right utilisation and protection of nature are built into it; such conduct takes from nature only per need and enriches in return. The three outcomes are one conduct seen from three sides — the Self, other humans, and the rest of nature — all harmonised by the same right understanding.

Q4. ANALYSING ONE ETHICAL SITUATION: during a group project, one member contributed almost nothing yet expected equal credit. MY ANALYSIS: (a) his INTENTION (to be secure, not to be shamed) is naturally acceptable — trust is not forfeited; (b) his COMPETENCE/commitment was lacking — a gap to be filled by guidance, not punished by exclusion; (c) right evaluation of MYSELF: my irritation was my own expectation of return. MY CONDUCT: I spoke to him privately (respect), clarified expectations (guidance), split remaining work explicitly, and credited all members while noting individual parts honestly (justice). RESULT: he completed his part, the relationship survived, and I felt no residue of conflict — the conduct was self-satisfying and people-friendly in one act.
